key_insight: A compact through-hole MHz transducer shortened Rayleigh-regime liquid jets, with threshold-like behavior in water and a distinct response in more viscous mixtures.
engineering_relevance: Nozzle-integrated acoustic actuation offers a compact way to tune liquid-jet breakup, though effectiveness depends on jet velocity, viscosity, and wetting.
method: Drive a through-hole lithium niobate transducer near its 6.7 MHz resonance.
Measure jet dynamics with 50,000 fps shadowgraphy and autocorrelation-based breakup-event analysis.
Fit a reduced-order threshold correlation to water forcing-amplitude and velocity sweeps.
evidence_signal: Experiments showed reduced normalized breakup length in water and glycerol–water jets, while the water response weakened as the Weber number approached 50.
watch_item: Wetting also shortened the jet, complicating attribution to acoustic forcing alone; sub-resolution mist and micron-scale atomization were not measured.
paper_title: Acoustic control of Rayleigh-regime liquid-jet breakup using a through-hole MHz transducer
